artifacts.summary: Research into the next-admissible-batch suggester: confirms all five dependencies (165, 272, 273, 275, 344) completed; documents orchestrate-batch-admit.sh v6's dependency-edge collision exemption (the mechanism the EDGE-PROPOSING STEP relies on), the --depends-on-add contract, the Move 5 conclusion-stage render point for Mode A, the commands/orchestrate.md queue-check call site for Mode B (and a file_scope gap there), the proposer/validator boundary with task 313, and candidate-pool/phase-map reuse recommendations.

memory_candidates.content: orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's collision scan excludes from its comparison set any task connected to the candidate by a dependencies[] edge in EITHER direction (the 'A1 dependency-edge exemption asymmetry' note in the script's own header). Adding a serializing dependencies[] edge via update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add is therefore sufficient, by itself, to flip a file_scope_collision defer verdict to admit on the next invocation -- no new admission logic is needed to implement an 'edge-proposing' remediation step; just add the edge and re-probe the real script.

In this repo's orchestrator, direction for a newly-proposed dependencies[] edge between two merely-territory-colliding (not inherently ordered) tasks cannot be 'inferred' from task numbering (multi-task-operations.md says so explicitly) but CAN be 'picked' deterministically (batch-orchestration-guardrails.md's rendering guidance) -- these are reconcilable: picking an arbitrary deterministic order (e.g. ascending project_number as predecessor, matching orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh's existing Class D display convention) is correct precisely because no direction is more 'true' than another for a genuinely unordered overlap; never claim the chosen order reflects a pre-existing truth.

scripts/roadmap-integration.sh's render_coverage_appendix() already groups ready (dependency-clear) tasks by wave and emits chunked /orchestrate N,M,... command blocks into ROADMAP.md's coverage appendix, but with NO file_scope collision check at all -- a real, pre-existing soundness gap, intentionally left for a separate advisory validator task (never this repo's machine-derived batch PROPOSER) to catch, per that validator task's own explicit 'this is a validator, never a proposer' / 'machine-derived batch selection is the proposer task's territory' framing. When two tasks in one repo both touch batch-suggestion-shaped work, check for exactly this kind of deliberate proposer/validator split before assuming overlap implies a missing dependency edge.
